body.statement: Von Kugelgen et al. (2023), Theorem 3.2, treats the bivariate case with one perfect stochastic intervention per node under a continuous witness genericity condition, whereas Theorem 3.4 treats arbitrary dimension using paired perfect stochastic interventions per node; the discussion entitled ``Identifiability From One Intervention per Node for Any \(n\)'' presents the arbitrary-dimensional one-intervention extension as a conjecture.

source.locator: Theorems 3.2 and 3.4; Section 7, paragraph entitled `Identifiability From One Intervention per Node for Any n'
source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 3.2 (Bivariate identifiability up to ∼CRL from one perfect stochastic intervention per node). (A2) we have access to a known observational environment e₀ and one single node perfect intervention for each node, with unknown targets. (A4) (“genericity”) the base and intervened mechanisms are not fine-tuned to each other, in the sense that there exists a continuous function φ. Theorem 3.4 (Identifiability up to ∼CRL from two paired perfect stochastic interventions per node). Identifiability From One Intervention per Node for Any n. We conjecture that Thm. 3.2 can be generalized to n > 2, subject to a suitably adjusted set of genericity conditions.

attestation.note: Main verified the primary NeurIPS 2023 PDF at Theorems 3.2 and 3.4 and the Section 7 discussion on 2026-09-06; transcription combines the exact headings and scope sentences with notation normalized from PDF extraction.
